payload.meets_need: Every pass line is demonstrated mechanically (run-82361b2e37e9: 165 tests, 163 pass, 0 fail, typecheck clean). Prop 1 trunk carries live claims only - after a close, trunk's tree holds no evidence, machines or state for that iteration, and none is left on disk. Prop 2 nothing is lost - every milestone's evidence is readable through iter/<id> after the close, asserted per milestone rather than only the last. Prop 3 work is durable mid-iteration - a blessed gate commits to the branch and leaves the tree clean. Prop 4 a false ship is impossible - an empty branch, an untaggable close and a conflict each refuse with trunk's HEAD unchanged and nothing pending. The folded need - a closed iteration stays listable - is met at the file level, with its honest limitation recorded as RAID rather than claimed.
payload.killers_demonstrated: S1 THE CLEAN CLOSE, S2 THE AUDIT, S4 THE SHIP THAT REFUSES: all three are exercised end to end by the ship-path scenario, in which an iteration is provisioned, walked through the loop and blessed at its final gate, and NOBODY calls shipMerge - trunk moves, the tag appears, the claim merges, the event does not, and the evidence is still readable through the tag. That scenario exists because filling S1 against the real system exposed that shipMerge had never been wired into the engine at all: it was invoked only from tests, which is the fuller reason i8c reported shipped while the repository recorded nothing. The close now runs on the bless path, so it works for every channel including the board.
payload.acceptance_converted: Converted and permanent, in tests/i5d-close-merge.test.ts and tests/imports-readonly.test.ts: the full ship path through the loop; the classifier in both directions, including that another iteration's evidence is not this one's event; milestone commits, and that an empty milestone is legal; the three refusals (empty branch, untaggable, conflict) each asserting trunk byte-identical; per-milestone reachability through the tag; the archive index surviving the filter; the toolchain installed rather than linked, and a shared install surviving a retirement; and four checks enforcing the read-only import law. Not converted, with reason: nothing here is owner-physical, and the one structural check (R7's wiring) is recorded as structural rather than dressed up as behavioural.
payload.consistency_swept: se.guidance-worktrees rewritten to teach the split, the mandatory-and-first tag, the refusal rule, the installed toolchain, and the grant index's role. The rule that matters beyond this repository is in there too: PUSH WITH TAGS, because the tag is now the only handle on an iteration's record and git does not push tags by default. Shallow clones are forbidden, partial clones are fine. The ADRs and the new law are the durable home for their own why, so nothing restates them at the application sites.
payload.gaps_logged: Three new: se.raid-closed-iteration-detail-unreadable (the honest limit - R12 proves the index file survives, not that any reader lists from it; i5e closes it), se.raid-mid-merge-crash-window (the working copy is not atomic even though HEAD is), se.raid-engine-iteration-cannot-self-demonstrate (an engine iteration's own ship runs under the previous engine). Carried: tags-not-pushed (owner, high), shallow-clone, audit-frequency, the battery flake, live phone pairing. Closed by this iteration: worktree-provisioning-incomplete.
